title: MAG-MISD: A Mode-Specific Adaptive Graph Framework for Multiscale Interaction and Station Dependence in Probabilistic PM2.5 Forecasting
content: Accurate regional PM2.5 forecasting requires models to capture nonstationary temporal patterns, scale-dependent spatial interactions, and predictive uncertainty. This study proposes the Mode-specific Adaptive Graph for Multiscale Interaction and Station Dependence (MAG-MISD), a probabilistic multi-station forecasting framework. Fixed variational mode decomposition separates each station series into five components, and a cross-mode Transformer contextualizes their histories within each station. The key innovation is to learn station dependence separately for each mode before mode fusion. For every mode, a directed graph integrates geographic proximity, persistent adaptive relationships, and sample-conditioned dynamic relationships, followed by bidirectional graph propagation. The refined mode representations are then fused and mapped to ordered conditional quantiles. Experiments using eight years of hourly PM2.5 observations from 127 Yangtze River Delta stations evaluate direct forecasts at 1, 6, 12, and 24 h. Compared with the same-input VMD-iTransformer, MAG-MISD reduces RMSE by 4.76%, 2.78%, 0.13%, and 0.72%, respectively, while consistently improving normalized Pinball loss and interval score. It also uses approximately 70% fewer trainable parameters. Ablation results support that station propagation, mode-specific adjacency, and particularly the persistent adaptive relation are the principal contributors. These findings show that modeling scale-dependent station dependence before mode fusion improves probabilistic regional PM2.5 forecasting efficiently.
